title: Nightmare Hope
text: “Even so… what in the world was that poison?”
“Sister… how foolish of her. But to think such a poison exists.”
“Yes… indeed. Melty, this is something I hadn’t told you, but there is a certain history between us and this poison.”
“Eh?”

From here, the Queen went on to explain about the Ouroboros deadly poison. At the same time, she also explained to us about the incident where another person had existed between Fiancée and the Crimson Swine, who had likewise died by poison.
“Motoyasu-kun.”
“I already knew about that from the loop, I say.”
After all, it was during the loop when I reunited with Fleon-chan that I’d succeeded in assassinating the Crimson Swine using a poison I’d made myself.
“Based on the Bitch’s testimony? That’s way too suspicious. I wonder what the truth actually is…”
Even for Father, it was a story suspicious enough to warrant doubt.

“Heard of it before. Vof, suspicious to the extreme. Being blamed on Siltvelt, unacceptable… It caused an uproar in Siltvelt too, and the culprit’s family was purged—a tragic incident. But even we never did figure out where they got a poison like that.”
Wolf too seemed to have heard of this incident before.

“For what it’s worth, when you put together all the various testimonies, it seemed difficult for that girl to have been among those who carried it out. However… I do feel that perhaps the truth lay elsewhere. It truly was a detestable affair.”
“The person blamed as the culprit on our side too… it was far too strange. That’s the kind of incident it was.”
The Queen gripped the hands of Tiger Girl, Tiger Guy, and Fiancée as though cherishing them, trembling all the while.
“Trash, it seems that it was that girl who killed Shizel after all. And now she tried to sink her poisoned fangs into this child as well…”
“Ngh… guuuuuuh!”

As though holding back his grief, Trash trembled and wept. It felt as though the truth had finally come to light. But there remained far too great a mystery. Should the truth be denounced here? Just as I opened my mouth to speak—
『Spear Hero, shut up, nano, or things will get complicated, nano. Naofumi, please ask Spear Hero to stay quiet too, nano.』
Rival warned Father and me via telepathy!
“M-Motoyasu-kun.”
“Ngh…”
“Bubu!”
Before long, Shadow Pig came dashing in toward the Queen. In its grip was a bottle that had apparently been found in the Crimson Swine’s room. …There was still something inside.
“That’s it, isn’t it. I can tell it’s something unusual, but… it’s hard to judge just from looking.”
Tiger Girl pointed at the bottle.
“Vof… just from the smell alone, it’s sweet? Claws can’t judge without a warning!?”
Tiger Girl and Wolf each testified warily about the bottle.
“It is that cunningly made a poison.”
“It was said to have been in a hidden cabinet in that girl’s room…”
The Queen handed the bottle over to Shadow Pig as it was.
“Analyze the contents of this bottle. But since it is a detestable thing, investigate it with the utmost care.”
“Bubu!”

And with that, Shadow Pig vanished from sight. Later, the investigation results confirmed it was without a doubt the Ouroboros deadly poison. An investigation was conducted into just where the Crimson Swine had procured such a dangerous substance, but in the end, it was too far in the past to determine, and it was settled that it had likely been a secretly hoarded poison.
“Heroes, thank you for keeping the damage to a minimum. Haah… and just when I thought things had finally settled down after dealing with that girl, this happens…”

The Queen too looked heavily fatigued. As for me, I could only say I was utterly baffled as to why such developments kept occurring. At the very least, I never imagined the Crimson Swine would die without me doing a thing! I say, it was ruined, absolutely ruined—I’d planned to make it suffer so much more, to torture it properly! Curse you, Crimson Swine! Dying to escape is nothing but cowardice, I say! I had fully intended to make it pay eternally, suffering endlessly, for what it did to poor Fleon-chan, who died in such agony.
“Well, we also, um…”
“I have no words other than to call it a pathetic end. If anything, it’s left me unsatisfied. I was hoping it might dance a little longer for us.”
Itsuki too seemed to feel a sense of indignation.
“…I never imagined she could be this foolish. In a way… perhaps it was for the best. If we think of it as her confessing to being the culprit before causing any more trouble…”
The Queen too seemed at a loss for how to respond.
“Heh… darkness has returned to darkness.”
“Hmm?”
Rafumi, isn’t that the exact same line Ren said back then? Kuro-chan tilted her head.
“Fangs of jet-black darkness. At times like this, you’re supposed to play along.”
“Got it—karmic retribution, own-goal, becomes instant death, becomes hazard, spreading contagion, which our darkness has stopped—Nightmare Hope, that’s what happened.”
“Kuro-chan, your word choices always seem a little off somehow…”
“Hmm?”
Black Thunder and Kuro-chan were similar, and yet sometimes just a bit different, I say. The Queen called out to Trash, who trembled beside Fiancée and Tiger Girl and the others.
“Trash, pull yourself together. This is not your fault. You mustn’t blame yourself!”
“Uggh…”
But Trash still trembled as though unable to accept reality.
“…Take Trash to his room. Atla-san, Fohl-san, Melty. Please stay with him for a while.”
“Understood.”
“Y-yeah.”
“Yes. Mother, um, is it alright if Filo-chan comes along too?”
“That’s fine. Please help him have such a good time that he forgets all about that girl. That is what Trash needs right now…”
“Yes. Heroes… is that alright?”
“Sure. Filo, go on ahead.”
“Got it—”
And so Filo-tan went off along with Fiancée and the others, taking Trash with them.

What left an impression on me was that Rival kept staring intently at Rafumi the whole time. In any case, as part of the investigation, the royal family’s living quarters in the castle were closed off for the time being, and it seemed an inspection would be carried out to confirm their safety.
That evening, a banquet was held, but the tension among the Melromarc side was low… making for a subdued gathering, lacking in any splendor.
“I’d call it melancholic, or maybe just a banquet in name only—kind of a buzzkill, isn’t it,” Itsuki remarked, giving his impression of the venue.

Of course, Father and the others put on a circus performance to try to liven things up, but since our side simply had more participants overall, it wasn’t quite enough to fully dispel the atmosphere. Still, I did get to see the Filolial Sage having a cheerful chat together with Fleon-chan and the Queen. Father’s circus troupe was lively too, and everyone seemed satisfied with the Filolials’ singing as well. Impressed by the idea of an entertainment meant to delight through song rather than battle or competition, the Sage came to understand that a circus could be a fine thing indeed.
“Ahh, isn’t there something more interesting? Somehow it’s lacking in liveliness.”
Itsuki egged us on, seizing the moment. Even while everyone was trying to liven the place up, he never changed his habit of finding something to complain about.
“Naofumi-san. Do something amusing.”
“Itsuki…”
Father glared at Itsuki with half-lidded eyes.
“Motoyasu-san, don’t you have anything either? If you two put your heart and soul into entertaining me with something funny, Naofumi-san, I might just forgive you a little.”
“I couldn’t care less about Itsuki’s forgiveness, I say.”
Why on earth would I need to entertain Itsuki, anyway?
“But well, let’s see… how about I share a bit of trivia that would ultimately work out in Father’s favor?”
“What is he planning to say… I’m a little uneasy about this.”
A charming little fact about Father suddenly came to mind.

“Father, that phrase you use when denouncing me or Itsuki—‘makura-arashi’—is actually a misunderstanding, isn’t it? I believe ‘makura-arashi’ properly refers to a courtesan stealing a customer’s wallet, and the correct term you’re looking for is ‘makura-sagashi.’ Perhaps you ought to correct that, I say.”
